newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures close mixed in light trade.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures close mixed in light trade.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed an uneventful session mixed, as concerns ahead of Friday's U.S. payrolls data kept both buying and selling interest in check, traders and analysts said.

One Standard & Poor's 500 futures trader said March S&Ps shook off the bond market's weakness and rose near the session high of 783.50, instead of mimicking Wednesday's 22-point decline in the last hour of trade.
However, the U.S. bond's market reaction to the January labor data, due out at 0830 EST/1330 GMT, will be critical for the S&P 500 market, they said.
Jerry Hegarty, an analyst with Thomson Research Publications, noted S&P futures opened down more than nine points on six of the last 11 employment days.
While traders are technically divided on the near-term direction of the bond market, almost all expect the data to generate volatility in both bonds and stocks.
Payrolls are expected to rise 237,000 in January, from a 262,000 rise in December, and the unemployment rate is seen easing to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent.
Nikkei futures, meanwhile, are expected to continue to decline, as March tested the 18,000 support level.
March S&Ps gravitated between 776.60 and 783.50, inside a wider consolidative band that some analysts had carved out between 785.00 and 774.00.
No arbitrage buy or sell programs were reported on the trading floor.

Fair value based on the LIBOR rate was quoted at 3.11 points, according to one floor trader. Arbitrage buy programs were seen at 3.91 points over cash, with arbitrage sell programs at a 2.31 point premium.

"The programs have scared away a lot of the day traders," one analyst said, commenting on the market's recent pattern of generating choppy price moves and heavy program trades in the last hour of pit trade.
"It's much easier to bully the market in the last hour of trade," he said. "And the momentum creates disparities against fair value and is then amplified when programs are hit."
He said March S&Ps have had a 4.5 percent correction since setting an all-time high at 799.70.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 2.15 at 782.65, Value Lines were 2.40 higher at 702.30, NYSE Composites were 1.95 higher at 411.30, Nikkeis were 140 lower at 18,080, Midcap 400s were up 1.80 at 263.70 and Nasdaq 100s were down 5.50 at 891.00.
